episodes.171151: A band of thunderstorms developed along a cold front during the mid afternoon hours. One of the thunderstorms knocked down trees & powerlines in the Boaz area. This same storm also tore metal roofing off of a building in that same area in Marshall County.
episodes.171194: Torrential rainfall, up to  2.6 inches was observed from southeast Denver and Aurora, and extended south southwest to Castle Pines, west of Castle Rock and into Roxborough State Park.  Most of the rainfall fell in less than 45 minutes.   A storm drain at Quincy and Parker was clogged up by rocks that got pulled out from near the sidewalk by running water. Several cars were towed out of the flooded area.  Minor flooding was reported on the Dry Creek exit of I-25 with standing water on Iliff Ave. near Buckley Rd. Parker and Quincy Roads and Dartmouth and Chambers Roads also were impassable.  Multiple accidents occurred due to the rain and flooding.  A few severe storms brought large hail up to quarter size, and strong winds from 60 to 65 mph in Arapahoe, Douglas and Elbert counties.||In Larimer County, flash flooding was reported In the Cameron Peak burn area along  Streamside Drive.  Dangerous flooding is occurring in the area of Glen Haven, including County Road 43 to Drake.  Highway 34 was closed from County Road 29 due to rockslides east of Drake.
episodes.171241: High pressure remained centered over the Southern Plains which allowed for monsoon moisture to continue to stream into western Colorado. This abundance of moisture resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms across the region. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain. Some areas in western Colorado saw debris flows and/or flooding.
episodes.171244: The plume of deepest monsoon moisture shifted over portions of western Colorado in response to a midlevel shortwave trough which tracked overhead. This resulted in an uptick in shower and thunderstorm activity. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain. Localized flooding and debris flows occurred across Montezuma and Gunnison counties.
episodes.171246: The plume of deepest monsoon moisture shifted over portions of eastern Utah in response to a midlevel shortwave trough which tracked overhead. This resulted in an uptick in shower and thunderstorm activity. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain. Localized flooding occurred in Grand County.
episodes.171642: Severe thunderstorms developed during the evening of the 14th with gusty winds in excess of 60 mph. Additionally, heavy rainfall resulted in street flooding for portions of Kimball.
episodes.171879: Morning convection produces waterspout across the coastal waters near Venice.
episodes.171920: A thunderstorm pushing offshore along the Martin County coast produced a strong wind gust.
episodes.172288: A narrow band of heavy rain fell across the I-64 corridor during the early morning hours of August 15th. The Charleston airport reported 4.33 inches of rain had fallen since the previous evening, with radar estimates ranging from 2 to 5 inches from Putnam to Fayette Counties. This was the result of a weak boundary tracking along an upper level disturbance, with an axis of showers and storms that propagated slowly eastward overnight. The Campbells Creek area of Kanawha County observed significant damage from flash flooding, with damage costs extending close to one million dollars. Flash flooding was also observed in the Scrabble Creek area of Fayette County. The Governor of West Virginia declared a State of Emergency for Kanawha and Fayette Counties due to the flooding, and recovery and clean up efforts spanned weeks after the event occurred.||Another round of showers and storms transpired on the afternoon of August 16th, which once again caused high water issues within Fayette County.
episodes.172337: A severe thunderstorm produced a very high wind gust at the Miles City Airport.
episodes.172433: Thunderstorms developed along a frontal boundary over north central into southwest North Dakota. One storm became severe over far north central North Dakota, with one inch diameter hail reported in Rolette County.
episodes.172450: Thunderstorms produced wind damage and hail.
episodes.172580: A storm tracked southeast from Kentucky into southwest Virginia near midnight, and blew down a few trees.
episodes.172581: A storm tracked southeast from Kentucky into southwest Virginia and northeast Tennessee overnight, and blew down a few trees.
episodes.172783: A few strong to severe storms developed right along the Palmer Divide in northern El Paso County during the afternoon of August 15th. As the storms slowly drifted east-southeast they became severe producing large damaging hail and pockets of flash flooding.
episodes.173112: An upper level disturbance passed southeast along a stationary front draped across central West Virginia during the early morning of August 15th, triggering strong thunderstorms that produced heavy rain across the central portion of the state. Toward dawn, the storms propagated farther east, and entered western Greenbrier County where it produced 1.5 to 2.5 inch rainfall totals, falling at times at a rate of around one inch per hour.  The rainfall registered as less than a 10-year average recurrence interval at all time duration.  Regardless, flash flooding was observed when Big Clear Creek flooded out of its banks and flowed across Highway 60 over 6 inches deep.
episodes.173210: Thunderstorms developed in the evening across Wyoming and moved eastward into western Nebraska through the late evening to overnight hours. A few isolated storms became severe.
episodes.173262: Abundant moisture (PWATs 1.7-2.0) and instability (MUCAPE 2,000 J/kg) provided a favorable environment for strong to severe thunderstorms across south-central Arizona on the 14th. Daytime heating aided in thunderstorm development across the high terrain north of Phoenix before sending outflows traveling toward the south into the lower elevations. New thunderstorm development occurred along these outflows into the Valley where they produced damaging winds, dense blowing dust, and isolated flash flooding. Additional thunderstorm development occurred across southwest Arizona where better moisture allowed thunderstorms to be efficient rainfall producers, leading to multiple reports of flash flooding. No injuries were reported from this event.
episodes.173291: From August 11-14, thunderstorms produced gusty winds and localized flooding.
episodes.173334: There were three tornadoes this day in McLean County, all near Ruso and in less than a one hour period of time. Thunderstorms developed along a variety of weak surface boundaries over southwest and central North Dakota as a weak short-wave trough passed through the area. One small area of storms developed along a very distinct surface boundary near Ruso in McLean County. In less than a one hour period of time three tornadoes developed. Initially, these tornadoes appeared to be of the landspout variety, but then two of the longer-lived tornadoes appeared to become supercellular as noted by rotation aloft which was shown during radar analysis. The first tornado was short lived and caused no damage and so was rated EF Unknown by NWS policy. The second tornado snapped hardwood trees and destroyed an animal shelter, and was rated EF-1 based on that damage. The third tornado developed while the second one was still on the ground, with both remaining on the ground for five minutes before the second tornado dissipated. The third tornado destroyed three small wooden granaries, flipped a large seed cart attached to an air seeder, tossed hay bales, flipped anhydrous ammonia tanks, and tossed hay bales, and was rated EF-2 based on the damage.
episodes.173340: Severe storms developed during the afternoon hours and produced large hail in the western Florida panhandle.
episodes.173368: On the 15th, the cold front made headway through northeast Arkansas, and afternoon temperatures were only in the 80s. It was still hot farther to the southwest, with readings in the 90s to around 104 degrees. It was the hottest day of the year to this point at Little Rock (Pulaski County) as the mercury hit 104 degrees. It was also 104 degrees at De Queen (Sevier County), Fort Smith (Sebastian County), and Russellville (Pope County). The front was surrounded by plenty of moisture in the low levels of the atmosphere, and this fueled scattered afternoon thunderstorms. The storms unleashed strong to damaging winds in places. Between Hot Springs and Royal (both in Garland County), numerous trees were downed. There was some roof damage, as well as damage to a shed and a fence.
episodes.173545: A rare surface cold front tracked southward across Central Alabama on August 15th. The air mass ahead of the front was very unstable, with afternoon surface based CAPE values 3000-4000 J/kg.  Clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms developed ahead of the front, producing sporadic wind damage.
episodes.173577: Chuuk was on the edge of the ITCZ, which promoted the development of thunderstorms which created gusty winds and outflow boundaries that propagated away from the thunderstorms at about 35 knots, as estimated by satellite imagery.
episodes.173580: A low pressure system and surface front interacted with a moderately unstable airmass and enhanced shear to support the development of strong to severe storms across the southern Piedmont and Sandhills. The strongest storms resulted in some 1.25-1.5 inch hail across Richmond County.
episodes.173602: Much needed rainfall occurred over the Coastal Bend of south Texas on August 14th and 15th as an area of low pressure, that formed over the northwest Gulf of Mexico, moved inland. The low pressure area was close to becoming a tropical depression and the National Hurricane Center designated the system invest 98L. Bands of heavy tropical rainfall moved across Corpus Christi from the late morning into the middle of the afternoon. Locally heavy rainfall produced flooding of roadways across the city. Another band of showers moved across the same region during the early morning hours of the 15th. This caused flooding of roads again in Corpus Christi.
episodes.173644: Thunderstorms moved northeast across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. Heavy rain and flash flooding was observed west of Safford and a dust storm moved across southwest Pinal County.
episodes.173666: Scattered thunderstorms developed over western North Carolina during the afternoon. Several of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.173667: Isolated thunderstorms developed over upstate South Carolina during the afternoon and evening. One storm produced damaging wind gusts in the city of Greenwood.
episodes.173732: A trough over the SE Gulf of Mexico contributed to a moist southwest wind flow across South Florida. This led to the development of showers and thunderstorms over the southern Florida peninsula and adjacent coastal areas.
episodes.173733: Thunderstorms resulted in flash flooding over several days, which included Zion National Park.
episodes.173740: Thunderstorms from tropical disturbance produced wind gusts above 35 knots around Corpus Christi Bay on August 14th.
episodes.173741: As the tropical disturbance moves west into the Brush Country on the 15th, bands of showers and thunderstorms produced very heavy rainfall. This caused flash flooding in the Laredo area and over portions of the Brush Country. Rainfall estimates of 5 to 8 inches were widespread across the Brush Country with localized amounts of 10 to 15 inches over western Duval County and southwest Webb County.
episodes.173797: Persistent moist monsoonal flow fueled thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. Many storms produced flash flooding.
episodes.173911: Weak shear south of a wind shift boundary was sufficient enough behind it to have up to 40 mph gusts and some wind damage that was reported from an isolated severe thunderstorm.
episodes.173930: A decaying MCV remains over the eastern Mogollon Rim in the morning brought an area of showers and a few embedded thunderstorms remain. Otherwise, clearing skies allowed for increasing instability through the afternoon. This allowed strong thunderstorms to form that produced heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.173943: An unusual August cold front generated widespread rainfall in southwest Virginia and extreme northeast Tennessee.
episodes.173951: Deep monsoon moisture remained over northern Arizona which lead to strong thunderstorms and flash flooding.
episodes.175609: An area of tropical low pressure moved into Texas from the Gulf of Mexico. This low generated thunderstorms one of which produced a tornado in Frio County.

events.narrative: Localized flooding occurred 5 miles north-northwest of Mesa as a result of heavy rain from thunderstorms. 0.94 inches of rain fell in an hour.
Weatherflow site at Poenisch Park on Corpus Christi Bay measured a gust to 36 knots.
ADOT reported that SR 238 was closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
Pictures on Social Media showed that the road from Polacca to Low Mountain was washed out and impassable. The wash likely flooded to Tolani Lake.
Images showed a large tree toppled and leaning onto a home near Ocotillo Road and Arizona Avenue. No injuries were reported.

There were numerous reports of wind damage in Anthem at Merrill Ranch, including 35 plus trees uprooted, snapped, or with branches down. There were also reports of roof tiles blown off and a Gazebo that was lifted from one yard to another. No injuries were reported.
Significant runoff and street flooding observed near Kimball. Kimball Airport AWOS station (KIBM) measured 1.26 inches of rainfall in less than 90 minutes.

Multiple trees were reported down in the vicinity of 36th Drive as well as 24th Street between Avenues B and C. Images showed a large uprooted tree down on a camper while another large downed tree fell onto a car. Timing was estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.

A video showed a flood wave traveling down Pinal Creek in Six Shooter Canyon before overtopping a bridge along Six Shooter Canyon Road. Flood waters could be seen traveling down the road making the road impassable. No damage or injuries were reported.
Trained weather spotter estimated winds were 60 mph on the north side of Hay Springs.
A flash flood was observed in the Pine Creek Slot Canyon due to earlier heavy rain upstream on Clear Creek.

The FCDMC streamflow gage along 4th of July Wash exceeded alarm stage, impacting a downstream low water crossing along Agua Caliente Road. The gage peaked at a depth of 0.74 feet. No damage or injuries were reported.
A mudslide occurred along Interstate 70 at mile marker 66 near De Beque.
Images showed parts of Alamo Road washed out due to high flow over low water crossings. Timing and exact location estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Localized flooding occurred 6 miles southwest of Montrose as a result of heavy rain from thunderstorms. 1.25 inches of rain fell in an hour.
Images showed a semi-truck blown over onto its side on I-8 near milepost 50. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Received report on social media of gusts 50 to 60 mph.
Washes were reported to be running across SR 72 and McVay Road, causing impacts to the roadways. No damage or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in less than 1 hour caused flash flooding in Pima, AZ.  Highway 70 became flooded and impassable.
Several videos of major flooding north of Chinle were posted on social media.
Multiple instances of flooding were reported along SR 95 south of Quartzsite, impacting travel on the roadway. No injuries were reported.
Alliance Airport ASOS station (KAIA) measured wind gust.

ADOT reported that SR 95 was closed due to flooding near milepost 80. There were also reports of a couple of cars that attempted to cross the flooded road but were not able to make it across and had to be pulled out. No injuries were reported.
The stream gauge on Havasu Creek near the Colorado River showed a 5 foot rise (to 1500 CFS) in less than 15 minutes.  This flooding was downstream from The Supai Village.
SR 95 north of Quartzsite was closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.

A solo boater was travelling to Uman Island from Weno Island, islands within Chuuk Lagoon. Nearby boaters waiting for the rough seas and gusty winds to decreases notice a boat circling a spot between the islands of Fefan and Tonoas. National and State police found the boat had no operator, and later the body of the male boater was found floating in the water. It is assume that he drowned after the boater fell overboard. The observation taken at the airport on Weno Island recorded a gust of 34 knots around 0351Z or 1351ChST. This information was given to WFO Guam by WSO Chuuk.
Several trees were blown down.
A few trees were blown down.
Antares Road was closed.

Campbells Creek was inundated with water just before sunrise. Several homes, roads, and vehicles were flooded in and around the town. Recovery efforts lasted weeks within the community.||High water was also observed along several roads near Charleston, including Goose Hollow Road, Letart Lane, Sugar Creek Drive, Sissonville Drive, Point Lick Drive, Garrison Avenue, Spring Street, Bullitt Street, and Greenbrier Street. In Cross Lanes, New Goff Mountain road was flooded for a period of time.
Multiple roads were closed in and near Golden Valley, and one swift water rescue was performed.
Emergency manager reported street flooding at Everhart Road and McArdle Road in Corpus Christi.
Emergency manager reported street flooding at Tarlton Street and Blanc Courts near downtown Corpus Christi.

Water from an overflowing Smithers Creek spilled onto Cannelton Hollow Road in the town of Smithers. This resulted in extensive flooding of several homes and a few businesses located along Cannelton Hollow Road. Severe flooding was also observed in the Scrabble Creek area.
Emergency manager reported access roads on Interstate 37 were flooded near Labonte Park.
Emergency manager reported street flooding in area around McKinzie Road and Leopard Street to Interstate 37 where the right two lanes were flooded.

A trained weather spotter observed Big Clear Creek out of its banks and flowing across U.S. Highway 60.  The highway was temporarily closed until flooding of Big Clear Creek receded.  No damage to the highway was reported.
Public reported street flooding in the southeast part of Laredo.
Public reported flooding of streets in northeast part of Laredo.
Flooding was reported in farmland and along roads near the Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City. This wash flows west then south to the Little Colorado River.

A small EF0 tornado formed as a cluster of storms was moving northward through northern Frio County.  An NWS damage survey found a small tornado touched down along CR 2537 on the south side of Moore and then moved NW for about a quarter mile before dissipating.  Two residences on CR 2537 have roof damage, along with several trees that were damaged.  A neighboring property across the street had its fence blown down. Several items from the properties were thrown about a 100 yards.  As the tornado moved quickly to the NW, it appears to have dissipated along CR 2518.  Maximum winds are estimated to be 75 mph.

Tree down along highway 38.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding.  Several intersections were flooded covered in 6 to 12 inches of water, and resulted in several road closures.
County comms reported numerous trees blown down across the city of Greenwood.

This was the first of three tornadoes this day in McLean County, all near Ruso and in less than a one hour period of time. The tornado touched down in an open field east of Ruso and impacted no structures. There was no damage to evaluate. By National Weather Service policy the tornado is rated EF Unknown.

This was the second of three tornadoes this day in McLean County, all near Ruso and in less than a one hour period of time. Hardwood trees were snapped and an animal shelter was destroyed shortly after development. Based on the damage done the tornado was rated EF-1, with winds estimated to be approximately 110 MPH.
Several trees uprooted near the intersection of County Road 28 and County Road 77.

This was the third of three tornadoes this day in McLean County, all near Ruso and in less than a one hour period of time. The tornado formed in an open field and approached a farmstead, passing just to the west and south of it. Near the farmstead the tornado destroyed three small wooden granaries, flipped a large seed cart attached to an air seeder, flipped anhydrous ammonia tanks, and tossed hay bales. The tornado continued on south of the farmstead where it tossed multiple hay bales before dissipating. Based on the damage done the tornado was rated EF-2, with winds estimated to be approximately 120 MPH.
